item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-928ecba774dee6e3","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"During López Obrador’s presidency, Mexico recorded historically high violent-crime levels; most crimes were not investigated or resolved, and militarized public security was expanded, including transfer of formal policing functions to the Defense Ministry in 2022.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.6","3B.10","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2023 context; evidence summarizes conditions through 2022","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the military expansion and security-policy framework to López Obrador’s administration.","limitations":["The source does not establish that all violence was caused by presidential policy.","Some statistics predate 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-928ecba774dee6e3","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The administration substantially expanded the armed forces’ budget, autonomy, and civilian responsibilities; military personnel conducted security, migration, social-program, customs, and infrastructure functions despite a record of human-rights violations and near-total impunity.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","4B.4","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Relevant baseline and continuing policy context for 2023","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes the expansion and assignment of responsibilities to López Obrador.","limitations":["The report describes institutional patterns and does not prove personal knowledge of every abuse."]},{"source_id":"SRC-928ecba774dee6e3","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"A 2019 appointment strengthened the National Search Commission: it updated the disappearance registry, created an anonymous online reporting and statistics platform, and began developing human-identification centers; however, the UN committee criticized official passivity and reported only 36 enforced-disappearance convictions.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.7","3B.10","6B.2","6B.5","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Relevant institutional context entering 2023","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the CNB initiatives to the government and notes the 2019 appointment.","limitations":["The source does not quantify the effectiveness of these initiatives in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e702e575f3d8a1bd","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In 2023 the National Human Rights Commission found 28 cases of serious violations by National Guard and military personnel, including torture, extrajudicial executions, and disappearances. After the Supreme Court ruled military control of the National Guard unconstitutional, the president defended the Guard and said he would seek renewed congressional authorization; he also denied reported abuses.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.9","4B.4","7B.2","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the defense of the Guard, proposed renewed authorization, and denial of allegations to López Obrador.","limitations":["The source reports allegations and institutional findings, not a final judicial determination for every case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e702e575f3d8a1bd","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"In 2023, authorities criminalized or used disproportionate force against land, environmental, and protest defenders; at least five journalists and at least 13 human-rights defenders were killed, while new Pegasus surveillance cases affected Centro Prodh members and human-rights official Alejandro Encinas.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the conduct to Mexican authorities but does not establish López Obrador’s personal direction of each act.","limitations":["The source does not establish responsibility for each killing or surveillance incident."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e702e575f3d8a1bd","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"A March 2023 fire in a Ciudad Juárez migrant detention facility killed at least 40 people after detainees were reportedly left behind locked doors; the Supreme Court separately limited migrant detention to 36 hours and required adequate legal defense.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6","6B.8","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The detention facility was administered by the National Migration Institute under the federal government; the judicial safeguards were imposed by the Supreme Court.","limitations":["The source does not establish the president’s personal involvement in the facility’s operational failures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e702e575f3d8a1bd","start_unit":6,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"In 2023, the government recorded 12,031 new missing-person cases and 114,004 total registered missing or disappeared people since 1962. The Ayotzinapa expert group reported military involvement and institutional refusal to provide information; López Obrador expressed support for the army, criticized victims’ organizations, and announced a criminal investigation of a former special prosecutor.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.9","4B.3","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the president’s public responses and investigative decision to López Obrador.","limitations":["The source reports the expert group’s findings and does not resolve all underlying criminal responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e702e575f3d8a1bd","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"After the president ordered a new count of disappeared persons, National Search Commission head Karla Quintana resigned. Civil-society groups feared the revision would reduce official figures; the replacement appointment was criticized for insufficient consultation, transparency, oversight, and experience, and the revised total was lower.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.10","4B.4","6B.5","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.4","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the recount order and appointment process to the executive under López Obrador.","limitations":["The allegation that the recount was intended to conceal failure is reported as a civil-society concern, not established fact."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e702e575f3d8a1bd","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The Inter-American Court ordered Mexico to abolish arraigo and reform pretrial detention; in 2023 the UN Working Group repeated the demand. A judge’s detention after releasing a murder suspect was described by the federal public defender as an attack on judicial independence, while López Obrador continued publicly attacking courts when their decisions conflicted with his plans.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes repeated public attacks on the judiciary to López Obrador.","limitations":["The source does not establish that López Obrador ordered the judge’s detention."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e702e575f3d8a1bd","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The Maya Train continued construction despite environmental concerns and alleged noncompliance with environmental law. The government continued fossil-fuel investment through the Dos Bocas refinery, while a climate-displaced community evacuated in November 2023 had not received promised relocation and services by year-end.","question_ids":["1B.9","1B.10","5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","6B.6","6B.10","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the infrastructure, fossil-fuel, and relocation policies to the government under López Obrador.","limitations":["The source does not provide a full cost-benefit or implementation audit."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e702e575f3d8a1bd","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"A May 2023 health-law reform granted people without public insurance free access to health services, medicines, and other benefits through IMSS-Bienestar, but health-rights advocates warned that the institution lacked sufficient resources to guarantee access.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The reform was enacted by the federal government during López Obrador’s presidency.","limitations":["The source does not measure nationwide uptake or outcomes by year-end."]},{"source_id":"SRC-34ab005a20d355d3","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The 2023 U.S. State Department report found unlawful killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, judicial-independence problems, media restrictions, corruption, gender violence, and discrimination, while also stating that the government generally took credible steps to identify and punish officials implicated in abuses.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.7","4B.4","7B.7","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates the Mexican government during López Obrador’s presidency.","limitations":["The report is country-wide and does not attribute every violation or enforcement action personally to López Obrador."]},{"source_id":"SRC-34ab005a20d355d3","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The official disappearance registry listed 113,188 victims through August 2023; the Ayotzinapa expert report found military and other agencies withheld key information, and SEDENA refused to comply with López Obrador’s order to provide crucial records.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the order to López Obrador and the withholding to military and other agencies.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether the president effectively enforced his order."]},{"source_id":"SRC-34ab005a20d355d3","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Independent media remained active and internet access was not blocked, but officials including López Obrador publicly discredited journalists; the administration used a recurring 'Who’s Who in Lies' segment, while journalists self-censored because of government and criminal reprisals.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","6B.5","7B.1","7B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the public discrediting and weekly segment to López Obrador and his administration.","limitations":["The source also identifies criminal groups as major sources of threats and violence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-34ab005a20d355d3","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"The 2023 report records generally free and fair recent elections, government cooperation with UNHCR and humanitarian organizations, labor-reform implementation across all 32 states, and investigations or sanctions in some corruption and abuse cases, alongside continuing corruption and weak enforcement.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","5B.5","6B.2","6B.4","6B.5","7B.7","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"These were actions or conditions of the federal government during López Obrador’s administration.","limitations":["Some matters involve state governments or independent institutions rather than presidential decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-516d837c17b4371a","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The early López Obrador administration combined social investment and fiscal restraint with politically driven choices; its economic team initially communicated respect for central-bank autonomy and fiscal discipline, while the administration also cut budgets for autonomous agencies protecting elections and transparency.","question_ids":["4B.4","5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.6","5B.7","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Pre-2023 baseline; limited direct fit","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates López Obrador’s opening months as president.","limitations":["The document was published in 2019 and does not establish 2023 outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-516d837c17b4371a","start_unit":12,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Mexico preserved preferential access to the U.S. market through the USMCA transition and renewed its commitment to open markets, while the report identified persistent poverty, weak rule of law, infrastructure and education deficits, and unequal distribution of gains as unresolved structural problems.","question_ids":["2B.7","5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.6","5B.8","5B.10","6B.10","8B.1","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Pre-2023 baseline and external-constraint context","ruler_attribution":"The report credits the incoming López Obrador government and its representatives with the USMCA outcome.","limitations":["The report predates 2023 and does not measure López Obrador’s full-term results."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ddccc2278b691882","start_unit":1,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Mexico’s GDP grew 3.1% in 2023, within the Finance Ministry’s projected 2.5–3.5% range; quarterly growth slowed to 0.1%, with agriculture contracting and manufacturing flat in the fourth quarter.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The figures concern Mexico during López Obrador’s presidency; the source does not attribute the growth rate solely to presidential policy.","limitations":["The article reports preliminary INEGI figures and does not establish causal attribution."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fd459b0d5838eea2","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Mexico’s peacefulness improved 1.4% in 2023 for a fourth consecutive year and homicides fell 5.3%, but more than 30,500 people were killed, organized-crime violence remained severe, peace was still 14.4% worse than in 2015, and political violence reached a record with more than 170 political figures and relatives killed.","question_ids":["2B.8","2B.10","3B.6","3B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The indicators describe national conditions during López Obrador’s presidency without assigning all causal responsibility to him.","limitations":["The report is published in 2024 and uses aggregate national indicators; causal attribution is limited."]},{"source_id":"SRC-197436938a23a322","start_unit":60,"end_unit":62,"fact_summary":"A 2023 government truth commission investigation into abuses during Mexico’s 1970s–80s 'dirty war' reported that military officials hid, altered, moved, or destroyed documents despite a presidential decree granting investigators access; investigators nevertheless interviewed victims and uncovered remains of seven people.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023","ruler_attribution":"The investigation was established by the federal human-rights department under the López Obrador government; the reported obstruction was attributed to military officials.","limitations":["The AP report does not establish López Obrador’s personal knowledge or involvement in the obstruction."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-094c70ee68be4b95","SRC-bc135725bb8d76ab","SRC-c0aaf2cba618c818","SRC-d8d542f031405967"],"batch_limitations":["Several sources are historical, inaccessible, or provide only preliminary context rather than direct 2023 evidence.","The supplied documents do not materially address nuclear risk, arms control, proliferation controls, or AI, cyber, biological, and other catastrophic dual-use safeguards; related 1B questions therefore have no supported facts in this batch.","Many reported outcomes are national or subnational and cannot be attributed solely to López Obrador without additional causal evidence."]}
